05 / ABOUT

Curiosity, mathematics, and the physics of nature.

I am a graduate student in the Theory Division at the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, Kolkata, working in relativistic hydrodynamics and exploring the theoretical foundations of strongly interacting matter.

Academic background ↘ Research interests ↘ Research page ↗ Curriculum vitae ↗

01 / BACKGROUND

A little about me

I am a graduate student in the Theory Division at the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, Kolkata, where my academic interests centre on relativistic hydrodynamics and theoretical high-energy physics.

I am interested in understanding how the fundamental principles of physics give rise to complex collective phenomena. In particular, I am drawn to the relationship between microscopic interactions, mathematical structures, and the macroscopic behaviour of physical systems under extreme conditions.

For me, theoretical physics is an ongoing process of asking precise questions, constructing mathematical descriptions, and examining the assumptions that connect those descriptions to physical reality. I value the interplay between mathematical reasoning and physical intuition, as well as the careful comparison of theoretical ideas with evidence.

03 / INTERESTS

Questions that motivate me

01 / PRIMARY INTEREST

Relativistic hydrodynamics

Understanding how matter evolves when relativistic effects become essential, and how conservation laws and constitutive relations describe the collective dynamics of strongly interacting systems.

Fluid dynamics Transport phenomena
02 / THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS

Quantum field theory

Exploring the mathematical framework of quantum fields and their role in describing fundamental interactions, thermal systems, and the microscopic properties of matter.

Quantum fields Thermal physics
03 / MATHEMATICAL PHYSICS

Mathematical structure & physical intuition

I enjoy studying the mathematical ideas behind physical theories, from symmetries and differential equations to the assumptions that determine the scope and consistency of a model.

Mathematical reasoning Physical principles

04 / APPROACH

How I think about physics

I believe that progress in theoretical physics comes from combining clear mathematical reasoning with an understanding of the physical ideas a theory is intended to describe.

I am particularly interested in examining how assumptions enter a theoretical framework, what its equations imply, and under which conditions its predictions can be trusted. Working through a derivation carefully is, for me, as important as understanding the intuition behind the final result.

I also value the broader scientific process: learning from existing literature, questioning familiar explanations, discussing ideas with others, and remaining open to evidence that challenges an initial interpretation.

05 / PERSPECTIVE

Beyond individual problems

Beyond any particular research question, I am interested in the broader relationship between mathematics and nature: why certain mathematical structures describe physical systems so effectively, how simple principles can produce complex behaviour, and where the limits of our theoretical descriptions lie.

These questions continue to shape the way I approach physics, mathematics, and the process of scientific learning.

06 / CONNECT

Scientific exchange

I welcome academic discussions and exchanges of ideas related to theoretical high-energy physics, relativistic hydrodynamics, and the mathematical foundations of physical theories.
